lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 45, which stops screenshot uploads from failing when two pull requests upload at once.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what may come later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Each upload first asks GitHub whether the file is already on the shots branch.
Then one call commits the file, which moves the shots branch.
On success it prints the new commit's sha, just as before.
If another run moved the branch first, GitHub answers with a conflict, 409 or 422.
lines.say: If another run moved the branch first, GitHub answers with a conflict, four oh nine or four twenty two.

lines.caption: Only then does it wait, longer each time with a random extra, and try again, six attempts in all.
Any other error, like a bad token, fails straight away with no retry.
On PR #35, a verify job lost a screenshot because PR #37 was uploading at the same moment.
lines.say: On pull request 35, a verify job lost a screenshot because pull request 37 was uploading at the same moment.

lines.caption: Each commit moves the branch, so a clash is harmless: trying a little later works.
The step list below the diagram gives the same six steps in words.
The random extra keeps two clashing runs from retrying in step.
A new SHOTS_BRANCH setting lets a test use a scratch branch; CI never sets it.
lines.say: A new shots branch setting lets a test use a scratch branch; C I never sets it.

lines.caption: And a dry run still uploads nothing.
The PR changes one script, plus this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built from the failed run on PR #35, three tries in about six seconds.
lines.say: It was built from the failed run on pull request 35, three tries in about six seconds.

lines.caption: And it follows option 1 from the issue, the smallest of three fixes.
lines.say: And it follows option one from the issue, the smallest of three fixes.

lines.caption: Two loops of six uploads ran at once against a scratch branch; all twelve landed, one on its fourth try.
The sandbox can't write through GitHub's API, so a stand-in turned each commit into a git push.
Every printed sha held exactly the file that was uploaded.
A bad token failed on the first attempt, in under a second.
Six conflicts in a row gave up after 73 seconds.
lines.say: Six conflicts in a row gave up after seventy three seconds.

lines.caption: A dry run printed DRY-RUN and uploaded nothing.
lines.say: A dry run printed dry run and uploaded nothing.

lines.caption: A real clash through GitHub's own API was not run here.
A fresh review agent found no high or medium issues, and four low ones.
Each low finding is a trade-off the issue had already chosen, so none was changed.
The real test comes after the merge, when two pull requests next upload together.
The PR and the failed job it fixes are linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
This PR is the first, smallest fix.
You watch for any missing image in a verify comment.
Only if clashes persist would the bigger fix follow.
That fix would commit a whole run's files at once, and pin every URL to one sha.
In short: uploads now wait out each other, and real errors still fail fast.
